description.narrative:
IFEX is a global network of more than 100 organisations in over 70 countries around the world, dedicated to defend and promote freedom of expression and information as a fundamental human right.
IFEX has developed a new five-year strategy for the period 2025-2029. The strategy focuses on four thematic areas, each of them with an overall goal: 1) Right to information - The challenges of access to information, its circulation and integrity, are confronted. 2) Civic Space - Civil society enabled and civic space protected as it relates to Freedom of Expression and Information (FoE&I). 3) Safety and Justice - A safer environment for those exercising their right to FoE&I.

Insatsen avser ett kärnstöd till yttrandefrihetsnätverket IFEX om totalt 51 MSEK under en treårs period den 2025-2027. För denna period har IFEX utvecklat en strategi, med fokus på följande tematiska områden:
1) "Right to information" - med målsättningen att addressera de olika utmaningar som finns kring rätten och tillgång till information.
2) "Civic space" - med målsättningen att de som försvarar yttrandefrihet och rätten till information och de utrymmen som finns stärks och skyddas.
3) "Safety and justice" - med målsättningen att skapa en säkrare miljö för de som utövar sin rätt till yttrandefrihet och information.

The upcoming plan comprises the conitinuation of three key goal areas for 2025-2029:
Goal 1: Civic space - Civil society enabled and civic space defended as they relate to Freedom of Expression and Information (FoE&I) In response to the worrying trend of shrinking civic space, IFEX first has identified the 'attack vectors', including the adversarial tactics used to further curtail the space, including through legislation that criminalises civil society, the restriction of foreign funding, and the suppression of Civil Society actors and citizens' rights. This results in human rights defenders, land defenders, and journalists reporting on these issues facing great risk, harassment, surveillance, public slander, attacks, and organisational closure. Organisations (and individuals) operating in isolation in the most closed societies are at greatest risk of unchecked harassment and closure.
To contribute to this goal, IFEX will deliver on two objectives:
1.Support civil society to participate in civic space and 2. Promote and protect open civic space.
Goal 2: Access to Information - Strengthened freedom and integrity of information: Facing increasing authoritarian actors and states throttling independent sources and restricting channels in order to shape and monopolise the dominant narratives, marginalised individuals within communities are often the most impacted, experiencing restricted access to the internet, education, and information that reflects their own identities.
Aware of the power that the free flow of accurate information brings to communities,IFEX proposes to address to the following:
1. Protect and promote equitable and timely access to information and 2. Protect and promote accuracy of information.
Various levels of activities IFEX proposes in this area include pursuing advanced technology (e.g. Ethical use of Artificial Intelligence), undertaking judicial advocacy for both accuracy of and access to information, action for holding governments accountable for information integrity and accessiblity, strengthening capacity and knowledge in digital literacy and journalistic integrity, as well as countering mis/disinformation through promotion of factchecking platforms and processes.
Goal 3: Safety and Justice - A safer and more just environment for those exercising their right to FoE&I This is an area where IFEX has long engaged in, i order to promote a strengthen a normative environment and accessible protection practices for journalists, rights defenders, and those most at risk of violations for exercising their right to FoE&I due to their intersecting identities.
IFEX has articulated the following pursuit of sub-goals:
1. Promote and embed a holistic safety culture and 2. Advance equitable implementation of robust justice standards and practices
To this end, IFEX has launched a robust programme for journalist safety in collaboration with other international partners that delivers a more cooperative and holistic approach to achieve greater impact for journalists at risk, and more reliable information sources for communities. This programme has been piloted over the last twelve months in Latin America and Africa and will be grown and cultivated throughout the next strategy period as a comprehensive global safety net for journalists. /end of text/
